newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH BOND YIELDS SEEN HIGHER BUT GAP STEADY.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH BOND YIELDS SEEN HIGHER BUT GAP STEADY.

text.p: Bonds were expected to track a fall in U.S. treasuries and German Bunds overnight with early quotes suggested an eight basis point rise in the long-end yield but the gap over Germany was seen about steady, operators said.
The markka and money rates were seen stable.
The U.S. 30-year bond yield rose to 6.96 percent from 6.90 percent at Wednesday's close, and the German 10-year bond yield rose to 5.88 percent from 5.83 percent.
Concerning U.S. market participants was a sharp drop in the March U.S. trade gap -- a 19.3 percent fall to 8.51 billion -- a strong indication that the economy was still growing.
Ahead of trading, yield quotes on the Finnish nine-year bond maturing in 2006 rose to 6.16 percent from 6.08 percent, but the yield gap was expected to inch up two bps to 30 bps early on.

"I do not see much selling pressure, there was not much at yesterday's (stronger) levels, so why should there be any now," a bond dealer said. But one analyst said: "With the gap at this level, it is time for some profit-taking."
